items.title: Support firms for Angus Taylor to win Liberal leadership
items.description: Support is firming for Angus Taylor to topple Opposition Leader Sussan Ley, though her supporters still expect her to achieve a "good result".

items.title: Protesters march through Melbourne's CBD as Isaac Herzog concludes visit
items.description: A large crowd is protesting in Melbourne's CBD as Israeli President Isaac Herzog's concludes his visit to the city.

items.title: Aussie backyard icon now on the chopping block
items.description: Barbeques Galore has plunged into receivership, leaving question marks for its nearly 100 stores that employ about 500 staff.

items.title: Assange's brother backs exiled former ASIO spy amid Bondi gunman claims
items.description: Former undercover agent Marcus says he shared intelligence with ASIO about Bondi gunmen Naveed and Sajid Akram's alleged terrorism associations as far back as 2019.

items.title: Mother of autistic man starved to death in hospital 'satisfied' with damning investigation
items.description: Queensland’s health watchdog finds Stewart Kelly's 2022 hospital death was the result of systemic failures in care, particularly around responding to his complex needs.

items.title: New video shows elderly man's arrest began with a hand on a shoulder
items.description: New video obtained by ABC NEWS Verify shows in vivid detail the arrest of a 76-year-old man, who was later released without charge.

items.title: Michele Bullock frustrated by 'repeated questions' at Senate estimates
items.description: Reserve Bank governor Michele Bullock fires back at Nationals senator Matt Canavan after he accused her of "gaslighting" Australians over the state of the Australian economy.

items.title: Murderer Martin Leach had to fight for end-of-life wishes, coroner finds
items.description: An inquest into the 2024 death of double murderer Martin Leach raises questions about whether prisoners have a right to end-of-life care.

items.title: Cars underwater, trees torn down — Alice Springs flooding in pictures
items.description: Overnight thunderstorms left Central Australian rivers inundated on Thursday, with rapidly rising floodwaters submerging cars, ripping up trees and leaving multiple people stranded.

items.title: Teens respond to One Nation's surge in popularity in the opinion polls
items.description: Recent opinion polls have found that, for the first time, One Nation is the second-most popular party with voters, overtaking the Coalition. So what do teenagers think of One Nation and do they still trust the major parties?

items.title: Two Chinese nationals accused of foreign interference granted bail
items.description: Police allege the two Chinese nationals, who are charged with reckless foreign interference for alleged spying on the Canberra branch of a Buddhist association, are linked to a woman arrested on the same charge last year.

items.title: Former CFMEU delegate among three arrested in anti-corruption probe
items.description: The arrests were made hours before Premier Jacinta Allan faced reporters over separate allegations detailed in a new report that $15 billion in taxpayer dollars had made its way into the hands of criminals who had infiltrated the union.

items.title: Epstein files hearing descends into shouting matches
items.description: US Attorney-General Pam Bondi faces furious questions over the censorship of names in the Epstein files at a heated hearing before a committee of Congress.

items.title: James Van Der Beek will always be Dawson Leery. He embraced it with humour
items.description: James Van Der Beek's death has prompted wide-ranging tributes from co-stars and friends who praised his kindness and humour.

items.title: 'Large crack' found in $786 million bridge days before opening
items.description: Days before the official opening, the Tasmanian government's largest-ever infrastructure project hit a hurdle, with a large crack picked up in one of the Bridgewater Bridge's piers detected and fixed, documents show.

items.title: 'This is over for me, I'm done': Woman says man assaulted her on solo bush hike
items.description: A woman's solo hike through regional Victoria took a disturbing turn near Daylesford, raising questions about safety and police responses.

items.title: Chocolate recipes to share some love with the people in your life
items.description: Whether you are into Valentine's Day or not, these chocolate recipes are perfect for sharing some love.

items.title: $10m worth of cannabis plants allegedly seized on NSW property
items.description: Police allege the four people charged were cultivating a large-scale cannabis farm in the Riverina.

items.title: Man admits to taking nearly 200 photos up women's skirts in public places
items.description: A court hears a man took "upskirting" images of unwitting women and girls in shopping centres and his workplace, in Melbourne, Geelong and Ballarat.

items.title: Hospital maternity unit embraces call for workplace culture overhaul
items.description: Staff at the Toowoomba Hospital maternity unit will be implementing recommended changes to their workplace culture following an independent review.

items.title: Gardener accused of killing Darwin mum 'unfit' to face trial, court hears
items.description: A gardener accused of murdering a Darwin mum in her backyard in 2022 has been deemed 'unfit' to face trial. The case has been delayed while investigations into Joerg Kloepper's mental state and ability to plead were conducted.

items.title: Outrage over 'secret' plans to sell off pokies-free bowling club
items.description: Bowls Queensland has repeatedly refused to comment on its plans for the site, despite pressure from all three levels of government.

items.title: Feral camels searching for water descend on remote communities
items.description: Large mobs of camels are wreaking havoc in remote Indigenous communities as they desperately search for water.

items.title: PM condemns 'white supremacy ideology' behind alleged Invasion Day terror attack
items.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has condemned the "racism and hatred" and "white supremacy ideology" behind the alleged terrorist attack on the Invasion Day rally in Borloo/Perth last month.

items.title: Chris Minns positions himself as the anti-protest premier. Will it pay off?
items.description: By expanding police powers and allowing bans on authorised public assemblies the Minns government has made restricting protest a defining feature of its first term.
